entries.description: In this episode of All Things Policy, Vanshika Saraf and Abhishek Kadiyala examine what the war on Iran means for the November 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. The joint U.S. and Israeli strikes that began on 28 February 2026 have not become a campaign issue in their own right, with only 4 per cent of Americans naming foreign policy as their top concern by July. The conversation applies a test drawn from Iraq in 2002 and Afghanistan in 2010, which is that American wars seldom rank as voter priorities yet often worsen the issues that do. The episode works through the evidence, including inflation at 4.2 per cent, petrol at USD 4.65 a gallon, record-low congressional approval of 10 per cent, and the repeated collapse of War Powers Resolution votes. entries.title: #23 Gerrymandering and the New Rules of US Politics

Callais decision weakens protections against electoral maps that dilute minority voting power, making it harder to challenge districts through intent-based rather than outcome-based standards. The piece analyses how both parties increasingly treat redistricting as a partisan tool, drawing comparisons to India’s independent delimitation system.

entries.title: Why The Blockade Is Trump's Best Card
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Abhishek Kadiyala argues that a naval blockade of Iran is the Trump administration's strategically optimal move — it avoids triggering the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock while maintaining pressure, keeping congressional hawks satisfied and doves outmanoeuvred.

entries.title: Analysing US Congressional Oversight on the Iran War
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: This policy brief examines congressional responses to President Trump's military action against Iran, which began February 28, 2026. The analysis explores two institutional mechanisms through which Congress can exercise oversight: the War Powers Resolution (WPR) and budgetary appropriations authority. The brief identifies deep partisan and intra-party divisions, tracks multiple failed legislative attempts, and concludes that budgetary restraint represents Congress's most viable constraint mechanism.

entries.title: 35 US Lawmakers Just Moved A Bill That Could Upend Indian Techies' Careers
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: Brigadier Anil Raman examines a bipartisan congressional bill, co-sponsored by 35 House members, that would tighten H-1B visa rules and add domestic hiring requirements — legislation that directly affects Indian technology professionals and reflects the populist electoral pressures shaping Congress ahead of the 2026 midterms.

entries.title: The Iran Brief: US Congress and Trump
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala, Brigadier Anil Raman & Soren Dayton
entries.description: With the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock ticking, this episode examines why Congress has again failed to constrain Trump's military operations against Iran. The panel unpacks the structural weaknesses of the War Powers Resolution — including the Trump administration filing only classified reports. The core argument: the real obstacle is political will, not legal ambiguity.

entries.title: Three Things May Happen At The End Of The 14-Day Ceasefire (Or Earlier)
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description: Kadiyala maps three possible trajectories as the US-brokered Iran ceasefire nears its deadline: a negotiated settlement, a return to hostilities requiring fresh congressional authorisation, or an ambiguous freeze that leaves war powers questions unresolved.

entries.title: The Iran Brief: Why Is US Congress Failing To Stop Trump On Iran?
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala & Bhumika Sevkani
entries.description: Congress has repeatedly failed to constrain President Trump's military actions against Iran despite multiple legislative attempts. The episode traces failed resolutions invoking the War Powers Resolution of 1973 — sponsored by Tim Kaine, Thomas Massie, Ro Khanna, and Chris Murphy — and examines how partisanship, electoral incentives, and ideological splits (cutting across party lines) have shaped outcomes.

entries.title: If Trump Puts Troops In Iran

entries.title: US Midterms 2026: Could a Polarised Congress Threaten India-US Ties? | MAGA, Immigration & Israel
entries.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
entries.description:
America’s 2026 midterm elections could reshape the next US Congress — and the outcome may have major implications for India-US relations.
The rise of MAGA Republicans and progressive Democrats, combined with the retirement of several establishment lawmakers, could lead to a more polarised Congress with fewer moderates.
For New Delhi, issues such as immigration, foreign lobbying, trade, India’s ties with Russia and India’s proximity to Israel could become sharper political fault lines.
Could a more divided US Congress make the India-US relationship harder to manage?
In this episode, we discuss the possible impact of the 2026 US midterms on India-US ties with Abhishek Kadiyala, Research Analyst, Geostrategy Programme, Takshashila Institution.

entries.title: America Votes | What Are We Watching?
entries.author: Brigadier Anil Raman
entries.description: In this second episode of America Votes, the All Things Policy series on the 2026 US midterm elections, Brig. Raman speaks with Professor Ryan Williamson of the University of Wyoming about what the 3 November vote may reveal. The conversation focuses on President Trump's push to nationalise his party's campaign, the Republican tilt of the Senate map, strategic retirements and the growing weight of primaries. It also flags the races worth watching, from Maine and Texas to Alaska, Kansas and Iowa. The episode closes on three election night indicators. These are the uniformity of the swing, the gap between candidates and their party, and the seats each party wins per vote. The larger question is whether American elections still reward candidates or simply parties.
